title: The Princess Who Wanted to Get Dirty
summary: A princess tired of always being clean and combed discovers, out in the garden, a joy that no castle can hold.

scenes.text: In a castle with pink towers lived Princess Amapola. Every morning, three ladies bathed her, perfumed her, and combed her with a silver brush until she shone like a mirror. "Don't move, princess! Don't get dirty, princess!" they told her. Amapola had to sit up very straight, with her hands still and her dress without a single wrinkle. But inside she felt a giggle tucked away that wanted to come out and play. She looked out the window at the wet garden and sighed softly. "What if one day I got dirty... just a little?" she thought, with a naughty tickle in her tummy.

That afternoon the sky filled with clouds and the rain began to fall, pit, pit, pit, on the windowpanes. When the whole castle grew quiet, Amapola tiptoed down the stairs. Very carefully, she pushed open the big garden door, which went creeeak as it opened. Outside, the air smelled of wet earth and wide-awake flowers. The rain was already leaving, filling the garden with puddles that shone like little mirrors. Amapola took off her shoes, breathed in the fresh air, and smiled like never before. At last she was alone, free, with no one to tell her "no".

Amapola looked at the biggest puddle of all and, without thinking twice, jumped in with both feet together. Splash! The water splashed everywhere and wet her face, her dress, and even her nose. The princess let out a laugh so big it startled the little birds. She jumped again, and again, and again! Splish, splash, splish went her bare feet in the mud. She got her knees covered in mud, painted herself a mustache of dirt, and laughed until her tummy hurt. Never, never in her life had she felt so happy and so messy-haired.

Suddenly, croak, a little green frog hopped out of the puddle and sat on her muddy knee. "Hello!" said Amapola between giggles. A little dog from the garden came running, woof, woof, and started splashing with her too. The three of them jumped and splashed together under the last few drops. But then a voice called out: "Amapola!" It was the queen, her mother, standing at the door with her eyes wide open. The princess froze, all covered in mud, waiting to be scolded. The little frog croaked softly. The little dog hid its tail. And there was a long, long silence...

Then the queen did something no one expected: she took off her shoes, lifted her golden dress... and jumped into the puddle with both legs. Splash! "I was a little girl who loved mud too," she said, laughing. Mother and daughter splashed together until the moon came out. That night, all bathed and warm, Amapola climbed into bed smelling of soap and garden. "You can be a princess and still get dirty, my love," her mother whispered, giving her a kiss. "What matters most is that you are you." Amapola smiled, closed her little eyes, and fell asleep happy, dreaming of a thousand puddles to jump in.
